items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: I never found out where Brock or Bernard were from in the States or who they have come to Europe with. I should have been a little more nosy than I was, but I never did ask other people many questions about themselves.

ctx.x: We finished the season with two weeks at the Casino of Ostende in September, as we had done the year before, and Willie announced that he was not going to lead an orchestra anymore. But when we arrived in Paris Willie told me that he would contact me in a few days. Ted Field and his wife Evelyn decided to go to the States. Willie did contact me a few days after we returned to Paris and told me that he had a job to open in a big dance hall called the Coliseum.

Willie engaged Tommy Benford as a drummer. Also another trumpet player who had been in France for a long time who's name was Theordore Brock and a tenor man who was living in France for years named Bernard and was said to be the wealthiest Negro American musician in France. I never found out where Brock or Bernard were from in the States or who they have come to Europe with. I should have been a little more nosy than I was, but I never did ask other people many questions about themselves.

We opened the Coliseum in October with a French orchestra on another stand and there were about 30 dancing hostess's engaged for men who came alone which was run on the taxi dance plan, but we did not play like the New York dancing school bands had to play. Willie also raised my salary to one thousand francs a week which was quite a good salary in 1938. The band now had two tenors and two altos. Big Boy Goldie was not with the band and Fletcher Allen had been hired in his place.
